recap: Under the House, in a hall older than it, Darrow found what makes the stone grow frost: a black sliver shut in the wall beneath the row with a lid of new mortar, carried up the Steps in the House's own letter-satchel. story_so_far.darrow: Down the undercroft stair at the Mender's count, on his own leg, he found a painted hall older than the House, a script he knows and cannot read, and a kneeling knight with the light running up out of him. He followed the frost to its source and broke the mortar off a hole under the row: a black sliver, the same glass as the chip from under the lad's tongue, carried up in the House's own satchel. He could not lift it. The cold took his right hand to the wrist, and he left the thing in the wall when Maelis said up. He has sent his name down the Steps with Rae as surety for a lame grey mare.
story_so_far.wren-ashdown: She went first with the lamp both times and counted the stair both ways. Over the inner door she read the old hand aloud before the Mender could, and stopped halfway, and has read nothing since. Her tally had the satchel coming up heavier than it went down; she found the kitchen's pry bar off its hook; she carried the lid of mortar up and set it down like an egg. She has the alcove, the bar and the hole under nothing in her ledger.
story_so_far.maelis-vorne: She took him down at her count and brought him up at it, knew the way east before he asked, laid her hand on a handleless door and said to leave it, and breathed the cold at the far wall as if it were air. She stopped his hand once; the second time she waited to see if he would go, and said up when the frost reached his wrist. It is the second time she has seen a hand go into one of those.
story_so_far.hollis-garrow: He had himself carried to the head of the stair both nights, the lad's blanket over his knees, and told the Captain to look at the wall. He saw the hand before the man when they came up, and called for fire in the voice that carries over rivers. He wants to know who is told.
story_so_far.rae-thorne: She named the inspected cage light before it cleared the cloud, said what the almoner's satchel weighed both ways, and told Darrow of a grey mare at a dealer's on the Holloway that will not take a bridge forwards. On the gate wall she took her aye, plain, and gave him her midsummer crate in return. At first light she went down the Steps with his name for the mare.
story_so_far.benedek-orrin: He lies in the Grey Cot and says his oath at every bell with Hollis's hand round his, the frost on his mouth neither growing nor melting. The thing that makes it is in the wall beneath him.
story_so_far.mother-ione: She turned a key no Prior before her had turned, three nights running, and asked at the top of the stair only whether the Captain came up on his own leg. When they came up with his hand white she looked, and asked nothing.
story_so_far.ivo-marrant: He read the Captain's letter to Aldric at the bars, thanked him for the candour, and sent it down the Steps by one of his men. His fires burn on the lower terrace, and his men have had the House's lamp oil open on its way up.
story_so_far.aldric-vane: Three letters in blue wax have come up the cage from Calden; the last is answered, and the answer has gone down by a Confessor's hand. About twenty riders under a banner that is not grey are on the Holloway.
story_so_far.sister-pell: She rings the hours. Her glass on its strap counted the Captain's letter down the Steps and the riders on the road.

options: Tell the Prior everything: the black thing in the wall, the painted hall, the satchel.
Tell Hollis and the far cots' keepers first, and the Prior only after: his own people before the House's law.
Tell no one yet, and watch the stair.

title: His Own People

where.detail: on the floor of the infirmary hall by the undercroft door, beside Hollis; the Prior standing off; Maelis gone up the row

time: the same night, every lamp on the row lit
last_beat: "Get the novice who feeds the far cots. The thin one. He's the one who'll have to know where not to put his feet."

people.did: Told Hollis, low, what is under the row: the black glass in the rock, carried up in the House's satchel; agreed the far cots' keepers hear tonight and the Prior after.
people.now: On the floor by the undercroft door beside Hollis, his right hand laid on his knee where Maelis left it. The far cots' keepers are to be told tonight; the Prior after, at Hollis's asking.

facts.fact: He told Hollis first, on the floor, what is in the wall under the row and how it came up.
facts.evidence: He told Hollis there on the floor, low, with the Prior ten paces off and the whole row lit

people.did: Heard it like a scout's report; said it is under his lad and under all of them; set the order: the far cots' keepers tonight, then the Prior, and the Prior is to be told it was his asking.
people.now: On the floor at the stair head with the lad's blanket pulled straight, sending for the novice who feeds the far cots.

facts.fact: He said the Prior is to be told the keepers came first at his asking, because it was.
facts.evidence: and you'll tell her it was my asking, because it was

facts.fact: He wants the thin novice who feeds the far cots told tonight, so he knows where not to put his feet.
facts.evidence: He's the one who'll have to know where not to put his feet.

people.did: Let go of his hand, laid it on his knee, and told him he will tell the Prior himself and she will not be standing beside him when he does; went up the row past the Prior without a look.
people.now: Gone up the row. She will not carry it to the Prior and will not stand beside him when he does.

facts.fact: She said it will not be her who carries it to the Prior, and she will not be standing beside him when he does.
facts.evidence: It won't be me who carries it, and I'll not be standing beside you when you do.

people.did: Watched Maelis go, then Darrow, and still asked nothing.
people.now: Standing off in the lit hall with the undercroft key, having asked nothing; she has not yet been told.

now.against: The black sliver stays in the wall under the row, its lid broken off and known; the Prior has not been told; Maelis has walked away from it; his right hand is out of use for a week.
now.next: The far cots' keepers tonight; the Prior after.
